ordered_groups.rationale: Strong, repeatable probability-scale heterogeneity evidence: validation R-loss improved in all three univariable R-learner splits, and causal-forest permutation increased validation R-loss in all three splits. Penalized treatment interactions also supported it in all three splits, with two of three nominal univariable interaction screens positive. Missing treatment main-effect evidence lowers confidence about that nuisance role but is not negative modifier evidence.

Direct probability-scale evidence is weak: univariable R-learner validation R-loss gains were nonpositive in all three splits, and causal-forest permutation importance was positive in only one of three splits with mixed near-zero values. Two nominal univariable log-odds interaction screens and one penalized interaction split provide limited supporting evidence, while strong treatment and outcome main-effect selection concerns prediction rather than effect modification.
